title: Two cuts for colored tilings
summary: The same rectangular tiling can be cut in two places and related to circular tilings. Adding the two counts gives a product identity for generalized Fibonacci and Lucas numbers.

tasks.title: Split a row at a marked cut
tasks.claim:
∀ a b m n : ℕ, tiles a b (m + n + 1) =
    tiles a b (m + 1) * tiles a b n +
      (if n = 0 then 0 else b * tiles a b m * tiles a b (n - 1))
tasks.role: Partitions the row according to whether a domino crosses the cut after m+1 cells.
tasks.context: A clean cut allows the left and right tilings to be chosen independently. A crossing domino has b colors and consumes one cell on each side. If the right side is empty, the crossing case contributes zero.

tasks.title: Open a bracelet at the clasp
tasks.claim:
∀ a b n : ℕ, bracelet a b (n + 1) =
    tiles a b (n + 1) + (if n = 0 then 0 else b * tiles a b (n - 1))
tasks.role: Identifies the sum of the straight-board and clasp-crossing counts.
tasks.context: Cut the circle at the clasp. If no domino crosses it, the entire circle opens into a row. If a domino crosses it, delete that domino and count the remaining row. For a recurrence proof, handle lengths one and two separately, then show both sides satisfy the same recurrence.
